turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come in. What is the problem.

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, my right heel is paining badly. Since two months the first step in the morning is like a nail going in, and if I walk a little it eases itself. I think I've overdone it with the jogging.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Which heel.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, I got new shoes also, from our own shop, very stiff, and the shop is so noisy I can't hear myself think half the day.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Left or right. Answer that.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Right side. Only the right heel. Sorry, when I get nervous I talk all around.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Only the first steps, or the whole day.
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): First steps are the worst, especially in these new stiff shoes. If I stand long in the shop it comes back a bit, not the whole day.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Swelling or redness.
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No swelling, no redness. I checked every morning.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fall or twist.
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): No no, nothing like that. I run three to four km most mornings, then I am standing the whole day, I work in a footwear shop.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Night pain, yes or no.
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Will this need an operation? My neighbour had some heel surgery and she was in plaster, I am really frightened.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): I asked about night pain.
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh. No. It does not wake me. Only the morning, and a little after long standing.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any tablets.

[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Amlodipine 5 mg morning for the pressure, atorvastin 10 at night for the cholesterol, metformin 500 morning and night for the sugar. And only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning, my mother sends it from Pune.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): You miss any of them.
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Uh, the night one, the cholesterol tablet, sometimes I forget. The others I take properly. Is that dangerous, doctor?
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Take it every night. Do not skip. I will book a heel x-ray today, and you stop all running for six weeks.

[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): X-ray? Is it a crack? These shoes I started the same week the pain started, two months back, sole like a board. And if I stop running fully I will put on weight with the sugar, no?
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. Same week as the stiff shoes, pain settles after a few steps, no injury, so I am cancelling the x-ray. No test, and no need to stop running fully.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me press. Tender just on the inner side of the right heel. I don't see any swelling.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Ow, yes, that exact spot. Is it something bad inside the bone?
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): This is plantar fasciitis. Morning first-step pain, stiff new shoes, that tender spot. Not a fracture.
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Plantar fasciitis, ok ok. What should I actually do? Kindly tell me the steps, I will forget, and can I still jog?
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Calf and plantar stretches, morning and evening, hold twenty seconds, three times. Silicone heel insoles in the shoes. Jog on alternate days, keep it shorter than 4 km.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Will the stretch tear the heel? Our shop has gel insoles, are those ok? And should I stop the Ayurvedic powder?
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): It will not tear. Gel heel cups are fine. Continue the powder and your usual tablets, they are not for this pain.
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): Err, my feet feel dead after standing, is that the nerve? I feel like a wet rag by closing time.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): Numb, pins and needles, or just tired.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Not numb. No pins. Just dead tired, like a wet rag. Sorry.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): That is fatigue from standing, not a nerve problem. Do the stretches and use the insoles. If it has not eased in three weeks, come back.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Three weeks, ok. If it gets worse before that, what to do? I saw ice on the internet and now I am more scared.
[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): Ice after standing is fine, ten minutes. If it gets worse, come earlier. Otherwise only if it has not eased in three weeks. No scan, no injection.

spec.situation: Runner or shop worker with heel pain on the first steps in the morning for two months; new shoes mentioned; doctor suggests stretches and insoles; no tests.

traps.happens: The patient describes things in colourful or sentence-like speech ('I've overdone it', 'I can't hear myself think', 'a frog in my throat', 'my feet feel dead', 'I feel like a wet rag').
traps.label_rule: Every symptom name is a short clinical noun phrase of 1 to 5 words ('voice fatigue', 'numbness in both feet', 'tiredness'), never a full sentence, never starting with I/we/my. Pure idioms that are not symptoms ('I can't hear myself think' said about classroom noise) are NOT symptoms. The patient's own words stay in the cited turn, not in the name.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

features: doctor_changes_mind: the doctor says one plan, then changes it after new information; the label holds the final plan.
patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.

omissions.text: Pain is only on the right side / only the right heel.
Heel pain is not present the whole day; first steps are worst and it comes back a bit after long standing.
Pain began the same week the patient started wearing new very stiff shoes, two months ago.
Patient sometimes forgets atorvastatin 10 mg at night, while the other medicines are taken properly.
Doctor initially planned a heel x-ray and stopping all running for six weeks, but then cancelled the x-ray and changed advice to no test and not stopping running fully.
Doctor stated the diagnosis as plantar fasciitis and specifically said it is not a fracture.
Doctor advised there is no scan and no injection.
